questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce crash injuries?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What material should you look for in a protective jacket or pants?

options.text: Leather
Polyester
Light materials
Dark colors

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs fully while riding. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright
Slow down and lean the motorcycle
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and move across it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which surface provides GOOD traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement provides good traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
Gloves made of leather
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and gloves made of durable material. A baseball cap does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What does a DOT-approved helmet do?

options.text: Restricts your side vision
Can greatly reduce head injury severity
Is usually uncomfortable
Makes it harder to control the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly reduces the chance of serious head or neck injury in a crash. It does not restrict your vision or make riding harder.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It makes you look cool
It is too warm to wear in hot weather
It provides crash protection
It should not be worn while riding

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides crash protection
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket for protection while riding. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather and help prevent dehydration.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind
It should not cover your arms or legs completely
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather
It can provide protection in a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: It can provide protection in a crash
questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly but allow free movement.

questions.question: What is the best source of information for your specific motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual
A general book about motorcycles
Someone who has a different motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It provides specific information for your model.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: On a motorcycle, the accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
It looks good.
It does not have a chin strap.
It protects your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet does not limit your vision. A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet lets you see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: What should you watch for when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
Traffic coming toward you.
Noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. Cars may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces without warning.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up and skidding.
Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Apply brakes automatically.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lock-up and skidding during hard braking. It works by releasing and re-applying brake pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how it handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It is encouraged for new riders to get practice.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one drink, will you be safe to ride?

options.text: Yes, you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Yes, your riding skills will not be affected.
Yes, as long as you ride slowly.
No. Alcohol may still be in your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Alcohol may still be in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. The time needed varies from person to person. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What can lower your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride in spots where it is hard to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible and communicate. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show other drivers what you are doing. Look ahead and maintain space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing at all times when riding. Crashes happen day and night, so stay visible whenever you ride.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles you cannot see.
Trust your mirrors to see everything around you.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles you cannot see.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of being in a crash?

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Signal your turns, use your brake light, and stay in the correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Test the seat for comfort.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally since most bikes work the same way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride an unfamiliar bike, get to know it. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear shift pattern before you start riding.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may go slowly while looking for parking.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create several dangers. A driver may pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between parked cars.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: Their effects are stronger than either one alone.
They are less dangerous than either one alone.
Their effects are usually small.
They cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects are stronger than either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter and prescription medications, affect your ability to ride safely. When mixed with alcohol, these drugs become even more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Assume they have ridden a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have ridden a motorcycle before. Explain what to do.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are not controlling the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have ridden a motorcycle before. Explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to understand how to stay safe for both themselves and you. Never assume a passenger already knows what to do. Give them full instructions before every ride.
